clue.text: Kyle, we hear, is not gay

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word meant by kyle is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a kyle is a Scottish word for a narrow sea channel, which is a strait

explanation.surface: Someone reports a rumour about a man named Kyle's sexuality.
explanation.walkthrough: Kyle looks like a man's name, but it is the Scottish word for a sea channel, as in the Kyle of Lochalsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight is the everyday informal term for heterosexual, the opposite of gay.

clue.text: Discipline heartless, sadistic hooligan? Not half!

indicators.note: with its heart removed, the word keeps only its outside letters
not half means only one half of the word is kept, the front portion

blocks.note: taken as written, then its middle goes
taken as written, then cut to its first half

explanation.surface: A harsh disciplinarian is asked whether a violent thug is the right description.
explanation.walkthrough: Not half is also British slang for very much so, an emphatic yes, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a branch of learning or doctrine, a discipline as in a school of thought.

clue.text: Irene gently traps rat

indicators.note: the phrase traps the answer, holding it enclosed within its letters

blocks.note: letters running from the name into the adverb

explanation.surface: A woman named Irene catches a rodent with care.
explanation.walkthrough: Rat looks like the rodent, but it is the verb: to rat on a deal is to go back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to break a promise or go back on a commitment, which is to rat on it.

clue.text: Nutty Nina's going mad on Ecstasy

indicators.note: going mad means losing order and sense, so the letters scramble

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A woman called Nina behaves wildly after taking a party drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutty is informal for crazy, and insane means out of one's mind.

clue.text: Half the world is into hemp now

indicators.note: going into means the short word is placed inside the plant name

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
here and now: the present moment

explanation.surface: A claim that half the planet has taken up cannabis these days.
explanation.walkthrough: Hemp, the cannabis plant, sets a drug-taking scene, but it is just a word to put letters into; now means here, as in here and now.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemisphere is one half of the globe, divided by the equator or a meridian.

clue.text: Foolishly I dared to get sacked

indicators.note: acting foolishly means behaving without sense, so the following letters lose their sensible order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An employee confesses to a reckless act of daring that got them fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Sacked suggests dismissal from a job, but here it means plundered, as a city is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, which is what raiders do when they attack.

clue.text: Part of Yorkshire terrier

blocks.note: first meaning: the valley of the River Aire in northern England
second meaning: a large wire-haired dog breed

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about a Yorkshire terrier, a small breed, but the dog meant is a different, larger one named after the valley.
explanation.definitionFit: Airedale is the valley of the Aire in Yorkshire and also the large terrier breed that originated there.

clue.text: Join Ted and Viola together, perhaps

indicators.note: putting things together in some possible way suggests the two names are combined and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A matchmaker considers uniting a couple called Ted and Viola.
explanation.definitionFit: To dovetail is to fit parts neatly together, from the interlocking woodworking joint.

clue.text: Caught sight of boy and wept

blocks.note: a boy's name, short for Desmond
shed tears

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a young lad, and the lad burst into tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Descry is a literary verb meaning to catch sight of something distant, so its past tense means spotted.

clue.text: Good-looking and generous

blocks.note: first meaning: attractive in appearance
second meaning: large or liberal, as in a sizeable gift or reward

explanation.surface: A description of an ideal partner: attractive and free with money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means attractive in appearance, and also substantial or liberal, as in a reward that is generously large.

clue.text: Takes on warriors

blocks.note: first meaning: faces up to or confronts with courage
second meaning: fighting men of a Native American people

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like hiring soldiers; the two parts are separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means faces danger courageously; as a plural noun it names Native American fighting men.

clue.text: Being in Glamorgan is marvellous!

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follow, spanning their boundaries

blocks.note: letters carried across the end of the county name and the next two words

explanation.surface: A cheerful boast about how wonderful life is in the Welsh county of Glamorgan.
explanation.walkthrough: Glamorgan is a historic county in South Wales; the answer runs from its fourth letter into the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any living creature, and an organism is the biological word for a living individual.

clue.text: Newspaperman got endlessly around, tired out

indicators.note: without its ends means the word loses both its first and last letters, keeping only the core
worn out suggests something knocked out of shape, so the word before it is rearranged
going around means the rearranged letters wrap themselves about the kept core

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the word with its first and last letters gone

explanation.surface: A weary journalist who has been rushing about is exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of TIRED are shuffled to EDITR, and the O from the middle of GOT goes inside, giving EDIT-O-R.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the person in charge of a newspaper's content, so a newspaperman in that role.

clue.text: Minister tops unofficial votes

blocks.note: Jack Straw, a senior Labour cabinet minister when this was set
to poll a tree or animal is to cut off its top or horns

explanation.surface: A government minister comes first in informal opinion surveys.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was Britain's Home Secretary and later Foreign Secretary. Tops the polls is a stock phrase, but here tops is a verb for lopping heads.
explanation.definitionFit: A straw poll is an informal sounding of opinion, not an official ballot or vote.

clue.text: Mistress of house has talk with girl

blocks.note: an informal talk
a girl's name, as crosswords often use

explanation.surface: The lady of the house sits down for a gossip with a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatelaine is the woman in charge of a large household or castle, its mistress.

clue.text: Princess's command causes chaos

blocks.note: Di, Princess Diana, with the possessive s
an instruction given

explanation.surface: A royal decree throws everything into turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a state of confusion and lack of arrangement, much the same as chaos.

clue.text: Sovereign is pre-decimal

blocks.note: first meaning: relating to an emperor or supreme ruler
second meaning: the old British system of feet, pounds and gallons

explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was also a gold coin from before British money went decimal in 1971, so the surface reads as a remark about coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes an emperor's supreme authority, and also the traditional British measures used before metric and decimal units.

clue.text: Speech therapists initially take on voices and speech impediments

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters of the words it follows

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
voices as a verb, to say aloud

explanation.surface: Specialists in speech accept patients with voice problems and stammers.
explanation.definitionFit: A stutter is a speech defect in which sounds are involuntarily repeated, so stutters are such impediments.

clue.text: I'm getting information of no importance

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped
material as in data or facts gathered for use

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the facts they are receiving are trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Something immaterial is irrelevant or unimportant, having no bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: Old revolutionary, great Nicaraguan leader

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning, so the next word is turned over into a new order

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tribute to a celebrated veteran revolutionary who led Nicaragua.
explanation.walkthrough: Old revolutionary looks like a description of the man himself, the Sandinista guerrilla, but it splits into O and an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega led the Sandinista government of Nicaragua in the 1980s and later became president again.

clue.text: You and I are said to be behind explosion in African capital

indicators.note: being said means spoken, so the two pronouns are taken as the letters they sound like
being behind means coming after, so the pronouns follow the noun in the answer

blocks.note: the noise of a blast
the two pronouns sound like the letters U and I

explanation.surface: Two people are accused of setting off a bomb in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Behind also means responsible for, which drives the surface accusation.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangui is the capital city of the Central African Republic, on the Ubangi river.

clue.text: Beamer giving one a black eye

blocks.note: first meaning: something that beams or shines
second meaning: slang for a bruised eye

explanation.surface: Someone driving a BMW punches another person in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Beamer is slang for a BMW car, and in cricket a dangerous head-high delivery, but here it is simply something that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner is literally a thing that shines, and also informal slang for a bruised, discoloured eye.

clue.text: Rome shaken by soldiers' conspiracy of silence

indicators.note: something shaken is jumbled up, so the city's letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: The Italian capital rocked by a military plot kept secret.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is a standard crossword source for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Mafia code that forbids informing on fellow members, a pact of keeping quiet.

clue.text: Go up to a poor, loveless chap, confused and unhappy

indicators.note: love is the tennis score zero, a round letter, so without love one such letter is taken away
a confused, upset state means the letters are jumbled out of their original order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before one round letter goes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to go and speak to a lonely, miserable, penniless man.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is O because a nil score in tennis is called love; only one of the two round letters goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To approach someone is to move towards them or come up to them.

clue.text: Motorist finally sold Humber, perhaps

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word it qualifies

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the Humber is an estuary river in north-east England; perhaps marks it as one example

explanation.surface: A car owner at last parted with his old Humber motor car.
explanation.walkthrough: Humber was also a British car make, which suits the motoring surface, but here it is the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver is anyone at the wheel of a car, so a motorist.

clue.text: Short generally unorthodox, which can be irritating!

indicators.note: cut short means the word loses its last letter
unorthodox means departing from the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, before its tail goes

explanation.surface: A grumble that unconventional brevity tends to annoy people.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergen is a substance such as pollen that triggers an allergic reaction, often an irritation of skin or eyes.

clue.text: Enjoy chutney?

blocks.note: first meaning: take great pleasure in
second meaning: a tangy condiment eaten with food

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading it as one question about liking pickle; the verb and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to savour with pleasure; as a noun it is a piquant sauce or pickle like chutney.

clue.text: Wild pea lies right for the trellis

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the following letters run free into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that a straggling pea plant is best trained up a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: An espalier is a lattice framework on which fruit trees or shrubs are trained flat against a wall.
